01-feature-building.notes: All 24 pass the 5 hidden contract tests and their own suites (re-run under 6 hash seeds). Differential fuzz (3000 random graphs incl. cycles and duplicate deps) against a reference: only T mismatches. Mutation testing wrapped each submission's own implementation with 18 behavioural mutants (empty->None, skipped id/dup/unknown/self checks, duplicate-dep stall, list mutation, static priority, ascending priority, tie by reverse/id/readiness time, FIFO, reversed/truncated output, cycle->[] / no ids / over-broad ids), because cross-suite runs are dominated by message-wording assertions. Key separators: T's duplicate-dependency bug (can return an invalid plan); RecursionError on cycles >~1000 nodes in I, J, Q; F's O(n^2) ready scan; cycle diagnostics that call downstream blocked jobs 'involved' (D, F, G, H, M, S, T, V, W, X; G/V/D at least label them as blocked). Close calls: B vs C (B only lacks non-Job validation); E/P/B at 9.75 ordered by mutation score then quality; G vs V nearly identical code, G ahead for its permutation-oracle test. Rejecting whitespace-only ids (L, N) was treated as a small contract deviation; rejecting float/bool priorities (E, I, N, Q, R) was not penalised given the int annotation. Not verified: anything about process beyond the folder (no process_note entries present).

D and K cap_drop ALL on redis (and K also on nginx) without the SETUID/SETGID/CHOWN caps the stock root entrypoints need; this is reasoned from entrypoint behavior because no images could be pulled. J's proxy probably also fails: on a read-only root as uid 101, nginx cannot create its default fastcgi/uwsgi/scgi temp dirs (moderate confidence). Close calls: C vs S vs T are all excellent; C edges ahead on the runbook (restore drill, variable-based rotation, known-gaps list), and S beats T on proxy hardening. O vs Q tied on total; O placed higher for keeping the Redis password out of argv and a loopback default. X's design is the strongest, but its scram auth-local setting breaks the documented backup path. U is ranked above J because its proxy handles all temp paths and it ships passing tests. Secret-leak failures: B, P and R have no .dockerignore while doing COPY . ., and R's RESPONSE claims otherwise. B also loses all forwarding headers on location / through nginx header inheritance. H's and D's base64 password advice breaks URL-embedded secrets (urlparse verified). Not verified: no image was pulled or built and no container was started, so nginx -t and actual entrypoint behavior are inferred, and runtime claims are reasoned from the configs. Compose config was rendered for all 24; C, J, Q, S and U fail on their shipped .env.example by design (empty passwords) and pass with dummy hex values.

06-product-planning.notes: OBJECTIVE_CHECKS.json was empty for every letter, and BRIEF.md and TASK.md were unchanged in every folder. All 24 PLAN.md and RESPONSE.md files were read in full. The deciding axis was how each plan reconciles the 24h post-acceptance purge with devices that may be offline when acceptance happens. C (submission-anchored Layer 2 cap), F/K/U (purge at confirmed submission) and P/Q/W (acceptance gated on purge) solve it by construction. Most others schedule the purge at accepted+24h on a device that may never learn of acceptance. Closest call: K vs U (both 9.5). U has the sharper milestone graph and ACs, K the cleaner product choice (no tablet merge dialogs, quarantine). K was ranked first on product judgment. P, R and X tie at 8.25 and are ordered by depth of risk reasoning. I and M lost milestone credit for calendar-like pilot schedules and unjustified headcounts. S lost credit for forbidden estimates and misreading the purge trigger. The task has no executable deliverable, so the conflict and purge designs were judged by reading them, not by testing them.

09-incident-analysis.notes: No input files were modified by any submission (cmp against _original_inputs). All customer updates are under 180 words per OBJECTIVE_CHECKS. No submission named a customer tenant (acme) in its customer update or blamed an individual. The main separators were: (1) fabricated rollout exposure ('100%'/'effectively all' eu-west: D, E, P, T, X, Q, J) and other unsupported facts presented as observed; (2) customer updates claiming no data loss, all jobs processed, or the US unaffected (C, D, E, F, J, K, M, N, O, P, Q, U, V, X to varying degrees); (3) diagnostic depth, meaning engagement with the falling-CPU vs zero-delay-loop tension, the active=10 vs 300 cap discrepancy, the unexplained 4-minute relapse, and amplifier vs initiator (best in U, M, H, D, O, G). Close calls: H vs B (both near-flawless on evidence; H's ordering analysis of the pool wait and broader hypotheses edged it); U/G/A tie at 9.25 broken by diagnostic depth (U > G > A); M vs R tie at 9.0 broken by M's stronger diagnosis and actions; O vs W and D vs N ties broken by diagnosis depth. S was marked down for a factual error (claims workers do not hot-reload flags, contradicted by LOGS.txt line 10). L lacks a required contributing-factors section. J asserts an incident date (2026-10-11) not derivable from inputs. Could not verify anything beyond the two input files; process notes in OBJECTIVE_CHECKS were empty apart from word counts.

13-frontend-playful.notes: Interactions were verified with a heuristic Playwright harness (water, undo, snooze, undo, complete all) plus targeted scripts for B, E, H, L, S and U, whose controls the generic heuristic missed. Close calls: I, T and Q all score 9.0; I is ranked first for its desktop 3-column composition and all-done forecast, and Q third because its detail panel visibly clips. K vs N vs O: K's shapes are the most distinctive, but it has a console error and an orphaned card; O is beautiful but relies on tiny, low-contrast text. Two submissions are functionally broken by CSS overriding [hidden]: L (a dialog that cannot be dismissed blocks all mouse input) and H (UNDEFINED status, empty chart, all-done always shown). A has the same [hidden] bug, but only on its toast. M and U were produced at reduced/low effort per their process notes; they are graded on output. I checked screen-reader announcements only by reading the markup, not with a real screen reader, and I did not check colour contrast with a tool.
